newsitem.title: USA: US experts warily eye growing herd of dollar bulls.
newsitem.headline: US experts warily eye growing herd of dollar bulls.

text.p: As more bulls pile on the dollar bandwagon that some hope will head past 130 yen, U.S. experts warned the greenback's rally may offer less potential for substantial gains past current levels.

"When that starts to occur, that again is not a sign that you're at a top but let's just say the risk-reward is starting to shift against you," David Solin, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics, said of the dollar's gathering strength.
Stampeding bulls pushed the dollar to successive highs against the yen Tuesday.
The rally was emboldened partly by belief the White House is not about to back away from its support of a strong U.S. currency, experts said.

Bulls trampled down resistance to prod the dollar to a 47-month high of 121.51 yen before midday, then retreated after rumors the Federal Reserve had checked rates for the Bank of Japan (BOJ). In late afternoon, the dollar rebounded to score a fresh high at 121.77 yen.
"Usually most long-term rallies need that last blow-out, and I think, we may be entering that phase," said Ron Leven, currency strategist at J.P. Morgan.
The rally may be good for another three or four yen, Leven said. While that does not mean investors should sell dollars now, he added, "I can't get on this 135-140 (yen) bandwagon."
